One chamber serves as a load lock and is equipped with a quick-access door, a transfer rod, an electrical feedthrough, a gas inlet, and a roughing pump.
After loading a sample, the load lock is pumped with a separate scroll pump to a pressure of p ≈ 10⁻¹ mbar within about t = 4 min before the gate valve is opened.

Axial motion of the transfer rod moves the sample from the load lock into the process chambers, while rotation of the transfer rod defines the angular position of the sample with respect to the deposition or milling sources, see Figure 4.
The load lock is separated from the main chambers by a gate valve.
Our design reaches a base pressure of p = 5·10⁻⁸ mbar without bakeout.
The required backing pressure is provided by a small scroll pump.
During standard deposition, the sample can be aligned facing one selected magnetron source.
Integrating ion-beam milling into the same compact vacuum system enables controlled material removal, surface cleaning, and subsequent deposition without breaking vacuum.
